en: The Hārati Stotra: Homage to the Goddess Śrī Hārati,
who resembles a kunda flower and is adorned with beautiful unguents.
I bow with devotion to Yakṣeśvarī, who possesses a vajra-body adorned with various ornaments, who dispels the suffering of fear with her lotus-hand in the right, and who has many sons. (1)
Her beautiful body is adorned with three eyes and embraces her sons with her own right arm;
she wears a crown fashioned from various kinds of precious gems.
I bow with devotion to Yakṣeśvarī, who has many sons. || 2 ||
Visualize her situated within a mandala of fire, upon a lotus of eight petals and a precious jewel-throne, with her lotus-feet placed thereon;
surrounded by Yakṣas and other beings, she sits in the graceful posture (lalitāsana).
I bow with devotion to Yakṣeśvarī, who has many sons. || 3 ||
To the one who pacifies the suffering of the three worlds, who bestows life upon children,
the illustrious Hārītī, who through compassion is skillful toward her own devotees,
and who removes the misery of those possessing enchanting enjoyments—
I bow with devotion to Yakṣeśvarī, who has many sons. || 4 ||
She who terrifies those of malicious conduct, who destroys the mass of afflictions such as boils and so forth for people,
who is like a mother to her devotees, and whose limbs are most cool.
I bow with devotion to Yakṣeśvarī, who has many sons. || 5 ||
Delighting in the Buddha’s instruction, possessing an exceedingly subtle form, with feet worshipped by the three worlds, consisting of the radiance of compassion,
and being attended by hosts of gandharvas and kinnaras—
I bow with devotion to Yakṣeśvarī, who has many sons.
Adorned with armlets, earrings, beautiful bracelets, and anklets, wearing various and variegated garments,
she is worthy of protection as she nurtures a multitude of children.
I bow with devotion to Yakṣeśvarī, who has many sons.

Day after day I remember her, whose full heart is intent upon bestowing the enjoyment of the realms of Svar, Bhūḥ, and Rasātala, and who is the very embodiment of the three *guṇas*; I take refuge in her.
I bow with devotion to Yakṣeśvarī, who has many sons. || 8 ||
A person should recite this hymn to Śrī Hārītī, the protectress, within their own home for the protection of children;
[she grants] speech, prosperity, very great happiness, and everything else.
He who, being self-restrained, recites this triad at dawn, [attains the fruit of] giving.
The Hārītī-stotra, which emerged from the illustrious Bhavaraṇa and provides protection for children, is complete.
